`document.cookie = "..."` looks like it replaces all cookies, but it adds or changes one. You build the string by hand: you have to encode the value and spell `path`, `max-age`, and the other attributes correctly, and the browser silently ignores what it does not understand. The Cookie Store API and cookie libraries take an object instead.

Only assignments are reported. Reading `document.cookie` is allowed.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```js
document.cookie = "theme=dark; path=/";
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```js
await cookieStore.set({ name: "theme", value: "dark", path: "/" });
```

{/* good */}
```js
const isDark = document.cookie.includes("theme=dark");
```

## When not to use it

The Cookie Store API only works on pages served over HTTPS, and older browsers do not have it. If you can use neither it nor a cookie library, turn the rule off.
